newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The government has given details and broad timetables for restructuring the transport industry for the first time, including the possibility that South African Airways SAA.CN might be fully privatised and listed within seven years.

- The Truth and Reconciliation Commission appears set for a conflict with the government over a proposal on reparations for victims of gross human rights violations which could cost between 270 million rand and 500 million rand a year for the next 50 years.

- New Africa Investments Ltd will take effective control of life group Metropolitan Life by swapping 10 percent of Sanlam's interest in Metlife for new Nail non-voting shares in a deal valued at 620 million rand.
- Gauteng provincial politicans and public servants will be asked to sign a public pledge committing them to paying for municipal services.
- Servgro shareholders approved the unbundling of its 3.7 billion rand food, leisure, transport and media interests, moving the parent company Sankorp closer to becoming a financial services group.
- A Pakistani shipping magnate has been convicted of the largest banking fraud in British history after siphoning $1.2 billion from the Bank of Credit and Commerce International.
BUSINESS REPORT

- French oil company Elf Aquitaine challenged continuing calls by the South African oil industry for an increase in regulated margins, saying the country's oil-refining margins were among the highest in the world.
- The possible privatisation of Eskom was thrown in the balance when the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (NUMSA) called for the electricity utility to remain 100 percent state-owned.
- The Financial Instruments Exchange (Finex) of the New York Cotton Exchange started trading rand-dollar futures on Thursday. The futures will be traded in New York and Dublin, the exchange said.
SAKE BEELD
- Financial markets worldwide will be keeping a close eye on the U.S. share markets, with further sharp falls possible on Wall Street.
- Sales of new motor vehicles fell slightly last month compared with February, but were still four percent higher than in March last year.
- The Cullinan group, which has suffered large losses recently, is busy with talks to merge its core business with another group.
- Russia will decide on April 15 about a contract with De Beers DBRS.Z on diamond exports.
BEELD

- Details of the acts and omissions by eight top ANC members alleged to have provided information to the apartheid government have apparently been presented to Deputy President Thabo Mbeki. The eight include four current ANC ministers, a provincial premier, a provincial party leader and two deputy ministers.
- Legislation is being proposed to force the liquor industry to take some responsibility for educating the public and help carry the costs of problems related to alcohol abuse.
- Weather forecasters are predicting a bitterly cold winter in the centre of South Africa.
- Expelled ANC rebel Bantu Holomisa held talks with National Party official Roelf Meyer about future political movements in South Africa.
